_comment: Deliberate divergences and runtime routines tools/fidelity.py honours when it reads a reference function's calls. skip: calls the port leaves out on purpose. lib: C runtime routines FID left unnamed (the port's copies are assembly with no PDB procedure to match), dropped like any library call. alias: a reference wrapper the port reaches through what it wraps. Every entry says why.

native.why: the codecs' SIMD kernels (dav1d's and libvpx's hand-written assembly) run as the reference's own machine code: src/gen/RefImage.cpp maps this range's bytes executable, and a call from translated code (the codecs' C side) goes to the address (tools/translate.py native_ok). They follow the Windows x64 ABI at their entry points, call nothing outside the range and import nothing (tools/translate.py checks each); no decompilation of them is C, and stubbed, the 63 the C side calls returned 0 (2026-10-18). Below 0x1400d0000 the range holds the anti-tamper runtime, which is never mapped.

libsodium's curve25519 field arithmetic (x25519, the login's key exchange): 44 routines entered from its C side (FUN_1420cc7e0) through six that take the Windows x64 ABI and translate, the other 16 passing state in rdi, rsi, rbx and r12-r15 between Ghidra's label cuts, each a register the decompiler lost (2026-10-18). Run as the reference's own code, whole; FUN_1420ca090 before it calls an import and stays translated. To 0x1420cc7c0, FUN_1420cc630's end: it is the inversion chain in the same style (rax the output, each helper's state in r13), and FUN_1420cc4a0 ends in a jump into its middle, so with the range ending at its start FUN_1420cc4a0 was refused as native and stubbed on `unaff_R13` (2026-10-18).

third_party.why: the protector's loader in front of the game: the PE entry point and TLS callback, 102 functions of obfuscated code with no strings, none of them called from outside the range (2026-10-18). Ghidra loses registers throughout it (31 lost-register stubs). The clean exe's game code never calls it, and FrostLite starts at its own entry.

the video codecs' hand-written SIMD assembly (dav1d's AV1 and libvpx's VP9 kernels, AVX2/AVX-512): 630 functions that call nothing outside the range, with no strings, entered from the codecs' C side. Ghidra cuts functions at labels inside them and their blocks pass state in registers, so no decompilation of them is C (469 of the 604 lost-register stubs, 2026-10-18). FrostLite decodes with libvpx built from source (vendor/libvpx-1.10.0, src/ui/MovieDecoder.cpp) and has no AV1 path.

third_party_names.why: the reference's own C runtime internals, named by FID and Ghidra (__crt_stdio_output::, __crt_strtox::, __acrt_*, common_*, the EH frame handlers, their lambdas): 297 functions, none called from outside the set (2026-10-18). Their templates and lambdas are not C (65 demotions and stubs), and FrostLite runs on its own runtime, the CRT's entry points mapped to it (tools/translate.py CRT_ENTRY).

the linker's delay-load stubs (`lea rax, <the import's slot>; jmp` the tail merge), which nothing calls (translated code calls those imports through their slots, the port's Import:: routines), and __chkstk, whose calls ApplyFacts makes nops (tools/protos.py): neither runs in FrostLite (2026-10-18).

more of the reference runtime's internals (2026-10-18): the language-specific exception handlers and vcruntime's rethrow filter, which only unwind data and the runtime's funclets reach (FID names the first `FID_conflict:__GSHandlerCheck_EH`), and the UCRT's _LocaleUpdate class, a member and so never dropped as runtime-only. Translated, they called __vcrt_getptd and __acrt_getptd, stubs.

skip.1402bd260: Aegis: the obfuscated per-thread copy of the current taint (lua_State +0x18) that anti-tamper checks compare with lua_taint; not ported, see vendor/lua-5.1.4/src/lblizzard.c
skip.1412c51b0: the small-block allocator's frame step (deferred frees per size class, a trim job every 600 frames): FrostLite allocates through the CRT and never sets up the heap at DAT_1430a8c70 (FUN_1412c46b0 is a stub), see docs/stubs.md

14063e310.why: lua_pcall behind an anti-tamper return-address check; the port calls lua_pcall (FrameScript.cpp, FrameScript_RunScript)

lib.1425bf3b0: memmove/memcpy (vcruntime): switch on the size for 0..n bytes, then 32-byte block copies
lib.1425bfa50: memset (vcruntime): the byte times 0x0101010101010101, switch on the size, then block stores
lib.14026bca8: _Init_thread_header (vcruntime): the function-local static guard over an SRW lock and condition variable
lib.14236a22e: the delay-load tail merge (the linker's __tailMerge_<dll>): the DelayLoad_ stubs jump here with the import's slot in rax, and it calls __delayLoadHelper2 (FUN_14254f840) on it. Translated code calls those imports through their slots, which tools/translate.py reads as the port's Import:: routines, so nothing reaches it; translated, it read the slot as `in_EAX` and was stubbed (2026-10-18)
